summary: Theodor Bloch was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch around 1888–1892, and later studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler around 1893–1895.

Theodor Goldstücker worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Königsberg and Bonn, and under Karl Rosenkranz, Peter von Bohlen, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1851/1852 to 1872.

Theodor Nöldeke specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and Theodor Benfey, as well as Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin. He held professorships at Göttingen, Kiel, and Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist. He studied at Leipzig under Georg Curtius and Hermann Brockhaus, and at Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe and Theodor Benfey. He held professorships at the University of Greifswald (1883) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the Hopkins School, Yale, and Princeton. He later served as president of Yale University (1831–1871) and president of the American Oriental Society (~1861–1870).
Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.
Theodorus Willem Juynboll was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Leiden University from around 1884 to 1893 and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.
Theophil Gubler worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Jacob Wackernagel and completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel by 1903.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied under Thanh Quý Chân Thật, at Báo Quốc Buddhist Academy, Saigon University, Princeton, and Columbia, later teaching at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh, and Cornell.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under the doctoral supervision of Shalini Singhal, attested in 2012.
Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou, later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies.

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of the West, where he studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge, supervised by Kottegoda Warnasuriya.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje), and later founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel works in religious studies and Indology. He earned degrees from Georgetown, Loyola University Chicago, and a PhD from the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, later serving as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University.

Thomas A. Tweed is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Stanford University, supervised by William R. Hutchison, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill from ~1993 to 2008.

Thomas B. Ellis is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Appalachian State University.

Thomas Berry was a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Indology. He studied at the Catholic University of America (~1944–1948) and held posts at the City University of New York and Fordham University (~1966–1979).

Thomas Borchert works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Chicago, studying under teachers including Bruce Lincoln and Martin Riesebrodt, and became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont.
